description: Machine-readable live work queue. Passing entries are retained for 24 hours, then removed by pnpm features:prune; durable behavior and evidence remain in product specs and Git/PR history. See docs/FEATURES.md for rules.

features.behavior: Row selection in the Rows table supports real bulk workflows: the "<n> selected" indicator gains a clear-selection (x) icon button, a select-all-on-current-page control sits in the header row above the first data row, rows can be selected by pressing and dragging the mouse rather than only one click at a time, and the CSV/download export honors the current selection - exporting only selected rows when any are selected, the full result set when none are.
features.evidence: PR #85 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/85), merged as 3bfde82. Implemented page-local row selection controls in RowsTable: header select-all-current-page checkbox, clear-selection icon button, pointer drag select/deselect across visible rows, and export button routing that downloads selected loaded rows as CSV when any are selected or falls back to the existing server-side full filtered export when none are selected. TablesTab owns the Blob download for selected-row CSVs. Verified locally with pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test, pnpm --filter @qyre/ui typecheck, pnpm --filter @qyre/web typecheck, pnpm verify:pr, and pre-push pnpm verify:pr. GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: The Schema tab's graph view reflects and lets you explore real relationships: MySQL foreign keys are introspected and drawn as edges (currently missing), disconnected node clusters get a visible explanation instead of silently looking broken, clicking a table or edge highlights the full relationship chain it belongs to, and MongoDB - which has no real foreign keys - stops rendering `_id` as though it were a relationship (currently clicking it navigates to a non-existent table showing no rows).
features.evidence: PR #86 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/86) merged as c2160d8. Implemented graph relationship-chain highlighting, disconnected-cluster/no-FK notices, and stable MySQL fixture FK coverage via qyre_demo_orders -> qyre_demo_users. MongoDB graph coverage confirms `_id` remains a primary-key column, not a relationship edge. Verified locally: pnpm --filter @qyre/web test; node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/mysql test; pnpm --filter @qyre/web typecheck; pnpm --filter @qyre/mysql typecheck; pnpm --filter @qyre/testing typecheck; pnpm check:quiet; pnpm verify:pr; pre-push pnpm verify:pr.

features.behavior: Switching the active database connection from the UI (POST /api/connect, F064) keeps every dependent view in sync: the sidebar/schema tree currently keeps showing the previous connection's tables/schemas until a manual reload and must refresh to the new target automatically, and MongoDB connections hide the SQL Editor tab entirely instead of rendering it as a disabled/greyed-out panel, since MongoDB has no SQL surface to disable.
features.evidence: PR #87 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/87) merged as 78912a5. Implemented explicit database-owned React Query cache reset/refetch after successful POST /api/connect, local workspace reset for stale selected table/file/query metrics while preserving the SQL draft, hidden unsupported shell tabs, and automatic move off SQL when the connected adapter reports supportsSql=false. Added isolated E2E coverage for switching from Postgres to MongoDB without reload: a Postgres-only table disappears from the sidebar, the MongoDB fixture appears, and SQL Editor is absent. Verified locally: pnpm --filter @qyre/web test; pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test; pnpm --filter @qyre/web typecheck; pnpm --filter @qyre/ui typecheck; node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm exec playwright test e2e/connect-and-inspect.spec.ts --grep "switching to MongoDB" --project postgres; pnpm test:e2e; pnpm check:quiet; pnpm verify:pr; pre-push pnpm verify:pr. GitHub CI passed End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: Cell values that look like an image URL or a plain URL get an inspectable preview (thumbnail/link) instead of rendering as plain truncated text; long raw-text cells past the truncation threshold get a distinct visual treatment (e.g. a color/background cue), not the same look as a normal short string; and the Files tab's "File browsing is disabled" message stops implying it's disabled because of the connected database engine - it's actually gated purely by the --files-dir CLI flag, independent of engine (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB/SQLite can all use it) - the message should say that plainly instead of reading like a generic, unexplained restriction.
features.evidence: PR #88 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/88) opened from feature/F086-url-cell-previews at c00289a. Implemented strict http(s) URL classification in the shared cell renderer, image URL thumbnails, plain URL link chips, URL inspection in CellValueDrawer with external-link and image preview affordances, and a distinct bordered muted treatment for long raw text cells. Updated the Files tab disabled copy to state that file browsing is gated by --files-dir and works across database engines. Verified locally: pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test; pnpm --filter @qyre/web test; pnpm --filter @qyre/ui typecheck; pnpm --filter @qyre/web typecheck; pnpm check:quiet; QYRE_DOCKER_BIN=/Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin/docker pnpm verify:pr; pre-commit format/typecheck/lint; pre-push pnpm verify:pr. GitHub CI passed End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: The Settings surface is rebuilt as a polished, scannable in-app configuration screen using the established Qyre/Fable visual language (docs/references/design-system.md) instead of its current one-off panel: sections are grouped logically, binary/numeric/list settings use the right shared-UI primitives, and persistence state (saved vs unsaved) is visually clear.
features.evidence: PR #89 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/89), merged as 060f6c7. Replaced the title-bar gear's one-off connection drawer with a full-screen SettingsScreen grouping Connection, Appearance, Layout, and Data & history sections; edits stage into a draft applied together on Save, with Discard restoring the baseline and the header showing unsaved-vs-saved state. Numeric fields clamp to bounds with a reset-to-default control; the gear opens Settings while a separate Database button keeps the connection switcher. Verified with pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test (130 passed), pnpm --filter @qyre/web test (21 passed), and pnpm verify:pr (checks, build, smoke + full E2E across PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB). GitHub CI passed.

features.behavior: `npx <connection-url>` (e.g. `npx mongodb://localhost:27017/qyre_test` or `npx postgres://...`) fails with npm's own EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL error because npx parses the argument as a package spec before qyre ever runs. The CLI gains an interactive guided-login flow for users who hit this or simply run `npx qyre` with no target: pick an engine, then enter user, a masked password (echoed as ****), host, port, and database; on a failed connection attempt, show the real error and offer retry (Y) or quit (N) rather than exiting. Startup help/output also explains the npx protocol:// pitfall directly and points at the correct `npx qyre <connection-url>` shape or this new interactive prompt.
features.evidence: PR #90 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/90), pushed as c283172. Added a `--login` flag that skips the connection-string argument and prompts interactively for engine (Postgres/MySQL/MongoDB), user, masked password, host, port, and database, retrying the connect attempt (Y/N) on failure. A target given directly with no username (e.g. `postgres://host:5432/db`) is now prompted for just the missing credentials, but only when stdin is a TTY, so piped/non-interactive invocations are unaffected. `--help` explains the npx protocol:// pitfall and points at `--login`; the no-target startup banner hints at it too. `connectToRaw` now also calls `adapter.ping()` after `connect()` (mirroring `/api/connect`'s own check from F085), since Postgres/MySQL's `connect()` only builds a lazy pool and would otherwise resolve against an unreachable host, defeating the retry prompt. New `packages/cli/src/guided-login.ts` (pure, injectable `GuidedLoginPrompts`) and `guided-login-io.ts` (real stdin/stdout wiring with raw-mode password masking and a persistent leftover buffer so a single chunk containing multiple piped answers isn't dropped past the first newline). Verified with `pnpm --filter qyre test` (44 passed) and `pnpm verify:pr` (checks, build, smoke + full E2E across PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB). GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: The Rows table filtering and table chrome are reviewed and rebuilt as a coherent cross-engine experience: operators and value inputs are derived from meaningful per-engine column capabilities rather than generic type strings, MongoDB BSON sentinels such as MinKey/MaxKey are not exposed as normal user-selectable filter types, invalid type/operator combinations are rejected consistently server-side, and the filter/table UI has clearer layout, hierarchy, spacing, and copy across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, MongoDB, and any registered engine.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test && pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test
features.evidence: PR #84 (https://github.com/ensp1re/qyre/pull/84), merged as 4f8ffe6. Implemented a shared browser-safe @qyre/core/filter-capabilities subpath that classifies engine-reported column metadata into meaningful filter capabilities and operator/value-input sets. The UI now receives the connected engine and uses that shared matrix to hide unsupported scalar fields, show only relevant operators, use boolean/date/time/datetime/number/ObjectId-appropriate value controls, and clarify filter/export copy. The server uses the same capability matrix to reject invalid direct API filter combinations before adapters run. MongoDB MinKey/MaxKey remain normalized for display but now collapse to structured object metadata instead of user-facing minKey/maxKey data types, and sentinel tokens are no longer coerced from scalar filter input. Updated rows-table-filtering.md to document capability-based validation and BSON sentinel behavior. Verified locally with pnpm --filter @qyre/core test, pnpm --filter @qyre/server test, pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test, node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/mongodb test, node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test, pnpm check:quiet, and pnpm verify:pr (checks, build, smoke E2E, full E2E across PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/MongoDB) all passing. GitHub CI passed both End-to-end and Lint/typecheck/test/build.

features.behavior: Product-spec pass for the role-aware permission/capability model before any implementation: create docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md covering the two-tier model (session-level ConnectionCapabilities extending F063's AdapterCapabilities with supportsRowMutations/supportsDdl/supportsIndexManagement/supportsDatabaseManagement/supportsTransactions plus a readOnlyReason of qyre-flag|replica|connection|grants|null, and per-table select/insert/update/delete TablePermissions attached to TableMetadata), the per-engine introspection matrix (Postgres has_table_privilege/pg_is_in_recovery/default_transaction_read_only, MySQL information_schema USER/SCHEMA/TABLE_PRIVILEGES + @@global.read_only, SQLite file+directory writability/PRAGMA query_only/mode=ro, MongoDB connectionStatus showPrivileges action sets), the advisory-introspection/authoritative-database principle with degradation to read-only on introspection failure, the API-shape decision (extend GET /api/overview vs a new endpoint - leaning extended overview), and how the UI adapts per access level. Follow the spec pattern of F063-F066. Architectural decisions are pre-settled in docs/exec-plans/active/0006-role-aware-database-ide.md; this spec turns them into a reviewable product contract with acceptance criteria.

Capability plumbing with no real introspection yet: @qyre/core gains the ConnectionCapabilities and TablePermissions types per docs/product-specs/permissions-and-capabilities.md (F090); DatabaseAdapter (packages/drivers/contract) gains a required getCapabilities(): Promise<ConnectionCapabilities>; all four adapters return their static engine truths (supportsSql as today, MongoDB column-DDL not-applicable, etc.) with the write/session tier hardcoded to read-only until F092-F095 land; the server exposes capabilities on the agreed API surface and re-reports them after POST /api/connect swaps the adapter (F064/F085); apps/web gains one shared capabilities hook in features/connection that all later write-UI gating consumes. A @qyre/testing-conformance case asserts every registered engine reports a well-formed capabilities object. No visible UI change. Depends on F090.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/core test && pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: Postgres permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reports real session writability (pg_is_in_recovery(), default_transaction_read_only, role attributes from pg_roles, has_database_privilege/has_schema_privilege CREATE checks), and getTable plus the batched all-tables path attach per-table TablePermissions via has_table_privilege(current_user, ..., 'SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE') batched per schema so no per-table round-trip storm is added. Introspection failure degrades to read-only with a logged warning, never to assumed-writable. Adds a restricted qyre_readonly Postgres user (SELECT-only grants) to the docker-compose init and @qyre/testing so integration tests cover both access levels from now on. Depends on F091.
features.verification: node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/postgres test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: MySQL permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reports session writability (@@global.read_only, @@session.transaction_read_only) and getTable/all-tables attach per-table TablePermissions by unioning information_schema.USER_PRIVILEGES, SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES, and TABLE_PRIVILEGES (a grant at any broader level implies the table-level right - the union must be tested explicitly since MySQL scatters grants across all three). Introspection failure degrades to read-only with a logged warning. Adds a restricted qyre_readonly MySQL user (SELECT-only) to the docker-compose init and @qyre/testing. Depends on F091.
features.verification: node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/mysql test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: SQLite writability introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() reflects whether the session can write at all - the database file AND its directory must be writable (WAL/journal files need directory write), PRAGMA query_only must be off, and a ?mode=ro/immutable open flag forces read-only; per-table TablePermissions are uniform (SQLite has no users/grants - the whole file is writable or not) and must say so via the capabilities shape rather than faking per-table variance. Tests cover a writable file, a chmod-read-only file, a read-only directory, and a mode=ro target. Depends on F091.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/sqlite test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: MongoDB permission introspection per the F090 spec: getCapabilities() and per-collection TablePermissions derive from connectionStatus{showPrivileges:true} - mapping find/insert/update/remove and createCollection/dropCollection/createIndex/dropIndex actions per db/collection resource (including anyResource and db-level wildcards); an unauthenticated local connection (no authenticatedUsers) is full-access, matching mongod's real behavior; introspection failure degrades to read-only with a logged warning. Adds a restricted fixture user with the built-in read role on the test db to the mongo init and @qyre/testing. Depends on F091.
features.verification: node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/mongodb test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: Qyre-level read-only session mode as the safety cornerstone, landing BEFORE any mutating route exists: the CLI gains a --read-only flag (mentioned in --help and the F088 guided-login flow) that forces the whole session read-only regardless of database grants; the server stores the mode in ServerContext and one central guard (a single choke point every future mutating route must register under, e.g. a route-config flag checked in a shared preHandler) rejects any mutating request with a structured error; capabilities report readOnlyReason 'qyre-flag' so the UI can explain itself; POST /api/connect preserves the flag across connection switches. Depends on F091.

Permission-aware UI shell: apps/web consumes the F091 capabilities hook - the status/title bar shows the session access level (read-only vs read-write badge) with a tooltip explaining why (Qyre --read-only flag, replica, read-only connection, grants), and capability-gating helpers land in features/connection for every later write surface to reuse. A new Playwright e2e asserts a read-only session (restricted fixture user and --read-only flag) renders zero write affordances - this is the standing regression guard every later write slice must keep green. Today's read-only visual experience is otherwise unchanged. Depends on F092-F096.

Product-spec pass for row-level editing before implementation: create docs/product-specs/row-editing.md covering the structured mutation API (typed JSON insert/update/delete-by-primary-key translated to parameterized SQL or MongoDB collection ops inside each adapter - the F072 filter pattern; the browser never builds SQL), row identity rules (full primary key required, composite keys supported, MongoDB uses _id; PK-less tables stay read-only in the grid with the reason surfaced), the pending-changes buffer + generated-statement preview + batch-commit model (transactional all-or-nothing on Postgres/MySQL/SQLite, ordered best-effort with per-op error reporting on MongoDB), the commit endpoint shape (open decision in exec plan 0006), value validation/coercion per column type reusing F082/F089 capability classification, the audit-event contract, and confirmation thresholds per docs/SECURITY.md. Depends on F090.

Structured row insert across all four engines per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: the adapter mutations namespace gains insertRow(schema, table, values) - parameterized INSERT on Postgres/MySQL/SQLite, insertOne on MongoDB - with value coercion per column type and the inserted row/key reported where the engine supports it. The server adds POST /api/tables/:schema/:table/rows, validating the body with Zod against the table's real introspected columns (same injection-surface pattern as F065/F072 sort/filter), gated by both the F096 central guard and the table's insert permission, and logging a structured audit event. Conformance cases cover successful insert plus rejections (read-only session, unknown column, restricted fixture user) on all four engines. Depends on F096, F098.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: Structured row update per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: the mutations namespace gains updateRowByKey(schema, table, keyMatch, changes) requiring a full primary-key match (composite keys supported; MongoDB matches _id), rejecting tables without a primary key, parameterized everywhere; zero-rows-matched is reported as a distinct outcome (stale row), never as silent success. Server route (PATCH on the rows resource) gated by guard + update permission, audited, with the same column-validation pattern as F099. Conformance across all four engines including restricted-user rejection and the 0-matched outcome. Depends on F099.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: Structured row delete per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: the mutations namespace gains deleteRowsByKey(schema, table, keyMatches[]) deleting only by an explicit list of primary-key identities (no filter-based bulk delete in this slice - that stays a deliberate non-feature until a spec revisits it), parameterized everywhere, MongoDB by _id list. Server route gated by guard + delete permission, audited with the deleted count; zero-matched keys reported distinctly. Conformance across all four engines including restricted-user rejection. Depends on F100.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: Batch commit for the pending-changes model per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: one endpoint applies an ordered set of staged inserts/updates/deletes - wrapped in a single transaction on Postgres/MySQL/SQLite (all-or-nothing; rollback on first failure with the failing op index reported) and ordered best-effort on MongoDB (per-op results with stop-on-error semantics per the spec). Adapters gain the transactional wrapper in their mutations namespace; the server validates every op against introspected columns and permissions before starting, and audits the batch outcome. Conformance: mixed-batch success, mid-batch failure rollback on SQL engines, MongoDB partial reporting. Depends on F101.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: The Rows table becomes an editable grid when - and only when - session capabilities and the table's permissions allow: double-click/Enter starts inline cell editing with type-aware editors reusing the F082/F089 filter value controls (boolean picker, native date/time/datetime inputs, number/text, explicit NULL setter, revert-cell), edits stage into a visible pending-changes buffer (dirty-cell styling) without touching the server, and editing is cleanly disabled - with the reason surfaced in UI copy - for read-only sessions, tables without a primary key, and non-editable columns per the spec (e.g. the PK itself). The buffer lives in features/table model state; commit wiring arrives in F105. Depends on F097, F098.

Permission-gated Add-row and Duplicate-row affordances per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: a new-row editor with the same type-aware inputs as F103, nullable/default-value handling, and per-column validation before staging into the pending buffer; Duplicate pre-fills from the selected row minus auto-generated keys (serial/identity/ObjectId) per the spec. Hidden entirely for sessions/tables without insert permission. Depends on F103.

The pending-changes workflow completes per docs/product-specs/row-editing.md: selected rows (F083 selection) can be staged for deletion when permitted; a commit bar shows staged insert/update/delete counts, previews the exact generated statements/ops per engine before applying, commits through the F102 batch endpoint with per-op error surfacing (failed op highlighted, buffer preserved on failure so work is never lost), and discards cleanly; deletes above the spec's threshold require typed confirmation. E2E: an edit-commit-verify roundtrip on one SQL engine plus MongoDB, and the F097 read-only guard stays green. Depends on F102, F104.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/ui test && pnpm --filter @qyre/web test && pnpm test:e2e

features.behavior: packages/drivers/contract gains classifyStatement(sql) labeling a single SQL statement as read | mutation | ddl | destructive (DROP/TRUNCATE always destructive; UPDATE/DELETE without a WHERE clause destructive; writable CTEs classify as their write action), extracted by generalizing assertReadOnly's existing comment/literal-stripping scanner so read-only behavior stays bit-for-bit unchanged - assertReadOnly is reimplemented on top of the classifier and its existing tests pass untouched. Pure text heuristic, defense-in-depth only; the authoritative gate remains engine-level enforcement. Unit tests cover the classification matrix including comment/literal/CTE edge cases. No server or UI change. Depends on F090.

Write-capable SQL execution per an updated docs/product-specs/sql-editor.md: Postgres/MySQL/SQLite adapters gain runQuery(sql) executing any single statement without the READ ONLY transaction wrapper, returning rows or an affected-row count, honoring existing timeouts and the F050 result cap (MongoDB keeps supportsSql=false, untouched). POST /api/query keeps runReadOnlyQuery exactly as today for read-only sessions; write-capable sessions route through classifyStatement (F106) - mutation/ddl statements run directly, destructive ones are rejected unless the request carries an explicit confirmed flag (a server-enforced round-trip, never client-only). Every non-read statement logs an audit event with its classification and affected rows. Server tests + conformance cover each class, unconfirmed-destructive rejection, and read-only-session behavior unchanged. Depends on F096, F106.
features.verification: pnpm --filter @qyre/server test && node scripts/with-local-env.mjs pnpm --filter @qyre/testing-conformance test

features.behavior: The SQL editor becomes write-capable when the session allows, per docs/product-specs/sql-editor.md: the results panel renders affected-row counts for non-SELECT statements; destructive statements open a confirmation dialog showing the classification and the exact statement before resubmitting with the confirmed flag (matching F107's server contract); UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE gets a persistent warning; query history records each statement's classification; and read-only sessions keep today's editor exactly, with a write attempt showing the friendly readOnlyReason instead of a raw rejection. Depends on F097, F107.

features.behavior: Product-spec pass for schema editing before implementation: create docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md covering the ddl adapter namespace (table lifecycle: create/rename/truncate/drop; column ops: add/rename/drop/alter type-nullability-default; index ops: create/drop), the per-engine DDL matrix - Postgres/MySQL native ALTER; SQLite's documented table-rebuild pattern for column drop/rename/retype (and which ops are native per version), preserving data/indexes/FKs in one transaction; MongoDB mapped to collections + indexes with column ops not-applicable - plus each engine's column type catalog exposure for the table designer (open decision in exec plan 0006: static list vs introspected), typed-confirmation rules for destructive DDL (type the table name to drop/truncate, per docs/SECURITY.md), and the API shapes. Depends on F090.

Table lifecycle per docs/product-specs/schema-editing.md: adapters gain the ddl namespace with createTable (columns with types from the engine's exposed type catalog, PK incl. composite, nullability, defaults), renameTable, truncateTable, and dropTable - MongoDB maps to create/rename/drop collection with truncate as deleteMany({}). Server routes gate on the ddl capability + F096 central guard, require the spec's typed-confirmation token for drop/truncate server-side, and audit every operation. Conformance: create-inspect-drop roundtrip on all four engines, restricted-user rejection, unconfirmed-drop rejection. Depends on F096, F109.

Server routes with typed confirmation for dropColumn, audit events, and conformance including a SQLite rebuild data-preservation case and restricted-user rejection. Depends on F110.

Read-only sessions see the structure information with zero mutation affordances (a strict improvement to today's read-only experience). E2E covers a column-add + index-create + drop-table roundtrip on one SQL engine, and the F097 read-only guard stays green. Depends on F111, F112, F113.

A read-only Roles & grants viewer so users understand why affordances are hidden: Postgres shows pg_roles plus a grants summary for the current user, MySQL shows SHOW GRANTS/information_schema privileges, MongoDB shows rolesInfo/usersInfo where permitted, SQLite shows file-permission facts instead; strictly a viewer - no role management mutations anywhere in plan 0006. Surfaces through the admin namespace with a capability flag; degrades cleanly when the connected user may not read role catalogs. Depends on F092-F095.

Conformance covers a denied insert/update/ddl per engine using the restricted fixtures with grants revoked mid-session where the engine allows.
